name: TX-20
label: Safe D

key_factors: San Antonio district with a strong Democratic partisan lean (D+16)
Incumbent Joaquin Castro running for reelection with a large fundraising edge
Republican challenger is minimally funded with no outside spending
Prediction markets price Castro near certain to win
model.rationale: Castro holds a D+16 seat, a decisive money advantage, and incumbency, while Baez has raised under $50,000 and drawn no outside support. Markets price Castro at about 98%, consistent with the fundamentals pointing to a Safe D race.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or Castro's underperformance relative to the district's lean in a strong Republican national environment would be the main ways this race tightens.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Joaquin Castro seeks another term in this San Antonio-based House district, which leans Democratic by about 16 points. He is a well-established incumbent who has consistently won comfortably, and he has raised more than ten times what Republican challenger Edgardo Baez has collected.

Baez has minimal cash on hand and no outside spending on either side, and no public polls or expert ratings track the race. Prediction markets give Castro roughly a 98 percent chance of winning. All available evidence points to a Safe Democratic hold, with the main uncertainty being turnout patterns in a low-salience contest.
